setupSteps: Pick the version. *Floor press (start here):* lie on a mat on a flat floor, knees bent and feet flat (Bodybuilding.com says knees bent or flat both work, snippet). Bent knees are the FitPlate default because they ease the lower back (coaching view). *Bench press:* a flat, stable bench that does not wobble; feet flat on the floor, wider than the hips for balance. *No equipment:* two filled bottles or cans, or a rucksack gripped by the top handle and strap, used in the floor position.
Floor. Non-slip mat, a clear 2 m x 1.2 m. Move furniture, fans and shelves; keep the area above your chest clear. Keep dumbbells close, one on each side.

Get the dumbbells into position safely. Sit with a dumbbell standing on each thigh near the hip, then lie back (or roll down) and use the knees to help lift each dumbbell to the chest, one at a time. This sit-and-roll method is common coaching practice; no authoritative source was found for the kick-up method: Not found. For heavier weights get a helper to hand them to you, and never lift more than you can place down safely.

Starting position. Dumbbells over the chest, arms straight but elbows not locked, palms facing the feet (or palms facing each other for a neutral grip, which suits shoulder discomfort; fitnessvolt and similar snippets).

Elbow angle. Elbows at about 45 degrees from the body, widest allowed about 60 (sources: 45 degrees in several, 45-60 in one; snippets). Wrists stay directly over the elbows, forearms upright when the dumbbells are low.

Shoulder blades. Draw the shoulder blades back and down gently and keep them there; the Noteboom et al. 2024 model study (barbell bench press) linked scapular retraction and narrower grips with lower rotator-cuff activity and lower shear forces (snippet; healthy experienced lifters, not clinical results).
Brace. Ribs down, tummy lightly tight, glutes gently on, head resting on the mat or bench, chin slightly tucked, eyes up at the ceiling.
Choose the weight. The lightest dumbbells that allow 10-12 slow reps with 3-4 clean reps in the tank (section 7). Many beginners need only a very light pair, or bottles.
Camera. Phone in landscape on the floor or a low stool about 40-60 cm high (est.), about 2.5-3 m to the side of your body, so the shoulder, elbow and wrist of one arm are in frame.
Warm up 3-5 minutes (est.): march on the spot, arm circles, shoulder rolls and a set of 8 empty-hand or very light presses.

steps.title: Get into position
steps.action: Lie on the mat with knees bent, feet flat, and the dumbbells resting on the thighs.
steps.feel: Back and head supported, feet pressing the floor.
steps.visualCheck: Side: head, upper back and hips on the floor, knees bent about 90 degrees. Front: shoulders level.

steps.title: Lift the dumbbells to the start
steps.action: Use your knees to help lift each dumbbell to chest height, one at a time, then press both up.
steps.feel: A firm hold with the shoulders low and pinned to the floor.
steps.breathing: Breathe out as you press up.
steps.visualCheck: Side: dumbbells directly over the shoulders; elbows straight but not locked.

steps.title: Set the shoulders and brace
steps.action: Draw the shoulder blades back and down, tighten the tummy, keep the wrists straight.
steps.feel: Chest slightly lifted, shoulders away from the ears.
steps.visualCheck: Side: wrists above the elbows; neck long.

steps.title: Lower the dumbbells slowly
steps.action: Bend the elbows and lower the dumbbells with the elbows at about 45 degrees from the body, until the upper arms touch the floor (or the dumbbells are beside the chest on a bench).
steps.feel: A stretch across the chest, controlled shoulders, nothing pinching.
steps.visualCheck: Front: elbows angled down toward the hips, not flared straight out. Side: forearms upright; elbow angle about 90 degrees (est.).

steps.title: Touch and pause
steps.action: Let the upper arms rest lightly on the floor for a short pause. Do not bounce or relax into the floor.
steps.feel: A brief stop with the muscles still switched on.
steps.breathing: Hold the in-breath only briefly, no longer than the pause.
steps.visualCheck: Side: upper arm lightly on the mat, wrist still over the elbow.

steps.title: Press up
steps.action: Push the dumbbells up and slightly together over the chest until the arms are straight but not locked.
steps.feel: The chest and the back of the arms pushing; no strain in the neck.
steps.visualCheck: Side: dumbbells rise in a smooth line back over the shoulders. Front: both arms rise at the same speed.

steps.title: Top position
steps.action: Pause at the top with the elbows straight but soft, wrists over the elbows, shoulders still low and pinned to the floor.
steps.feel: Chest slightly squeezed; no locking pain.

steps.title: Repeat for 10-12 reps
steps.action: Repeat from step 4 with the same depth and speed each rep.
steps.breathing: Out on the press, in on the lowering.
steps.visualCheck: Same elbow angle and path every rep.

steps.title: Set the dumbbells down safely
steps.action: Lower the dumbbells to your chest, then to the thighs one at a time, then roll onto your side or sit up, and put them on the mat beside you. Do not drop them from over your face.
steps.feel: Controlled, no sudden pull in the shoulder.
steps.visualCheck: Side: dumbbells go to the thighs first; no dropping.

commonMistakes.title: Flaring the elbows straight out (about 90 degrees from the body)
commonMistakes.text: Flaring the elbows straight out (about 90 degrees from the body). Why: coaches link it with more front-shoulder load and more shoulder stress, and one source puts the line at about 45 degrees (AOL/trainer, boxrox, jeromybryk, snippets). Fix: tuck the elbows to about 45-60 degrees, "elbows pointing toward the hips".

commonMistakes.title: Too much weight
commonMistakes.text: Too much weight. Why: causes bouncing, uneven arms and a bigger arch (Livestrong, builtwithscience, snippets). Fix: choose by 3-4 reps in reserve (section 7); a bottle is a normal start.

commonMistakes.title: Bouncing the upper arms off the floor (or the dumbbells off the chest)
commonMistakes.text: Bouncing the upper arms off the floor (or the dumbbells off the chest). Why: lose control at the bottom and jerk the shoulder (coaching view). Fix: touch lightly, 1 s pause.

commonMistakes.title: Arching the back and lifting the hips
commonMistakes.text: Arching the back and lifting the hips. Why: a common cause of lower-back strain (aaptiv, boxrox snippets). Fix: floor press with knees bent, ribs down, hips on the mat.

commonMistakes.title: Wrists bent back or hands wider than the elbows
commonMistakes.text: Wrists bent back or hands wider than the elbows. Why: strain on the wrist and an uneven push (Livestrong, AOL, snippets). Fix: wrists straight, forearms upright.

commonMistakes.title: Dumbbells drifting toward the face or too far forward
commonMistakes.text: Dumbbells drifting toward the face or too far forward. Why: loses the line over the shoulders and adds shoulder strain (coaching view). Fix: keep the dumbbells over the shoulders and press up and slightly together.

commonMistakes.title: Shrugging or letting the shoulders roll forward
commonMistakes.text: Shrugging or letting the shoulders roll forward. Why: removes the stable base (Noteboom et al., scapular retraction snippet). Fix: shoulder blades back and down.

commonMistakes.title: Not controlling the lowering
commonMistakes.text: Not controlling the lowering. Why: loses half the work and risks shoulder strain (coaching view). Fix: 2-3 s down.

commonMistakes.title: Holding the breath
commonMistakes.text: Holding the breath. Why: raises blood pressure and brings dizziness (PubMed 7741618, carried). Fix: out on the press, in on the lowering.

commonMistakes.title: Dropping dumbbells from over the face or onto the floor
commonMistakes.text: Dropping dumbbells from over the face or onto the floor. Why: danger to face and teeth, and noise below. Fix: lower to the thighs one at a time, then to the mat; lighten the load.

safetyNotes: Shoulder problems (impingement, rotator cuff, instability, past dislocation): the Noteboom et al. 2024 study (snippet) says no biomechanical evidence yet shows what lowers bench press shoulder injury risk, and one cited study found tendinitis in about 76% of strength trainers reporting bench-related shoulder pain (snippet). Use the floor press for a limited depth, palms facing each other if more comfortable, elbows tucked, a pain-free range, and stop with pinching or pain; ask a physiotherapist.

High blood pressure and heart disease: breathe out on the press, never hold the breath, very light weight; get clearance first with heart disease or uncontrolled blood pressure (PubMed 7741618, carried).
Lower back problems: use the floor press with knees bent, no arching, a light weight; stop if pain increases.
Neck pain: keep the head resting and the chin slightly tucked; use a very light weight.
Osteoporosis: loaded strength work is generally recommended; the floor press loads the spine little if the trunk stays still; with a vertebral fracture or severe osteoporosis ask a clinician.

Pregnancy and postpartum: ACOG's guidance as summarised by secondary sources advises avoiding exercise lying flat on the back in the second and third trimesters because of reduced blood flow (snippet); a 2019 systematic review found insufficient evidence either way (PubMed 30337348, snippet); another source says lying exercise causes problems mainly if you feel lightheaded or nauseous (HSS, snippet). Ask your obstetrician or midwife; an inclined or seated press is often used instead. ACOG's own wording: Not found.
Mumbai flat: mat under you, lower the dumbbells gently, keep clear of furniture and fans, no glass bottles, and never press over the face with anything heavier than you can control.

conditionCautions.change: Light weight, 3-4 reps in reserve, breathe out on the press and never hold the breath; avoid straining; check blood pressure is controlled; ask a doctor if readings are very high or medicines cause dizziness
conditionCautions.source: Harvard Health strength training and blood pressure (carried); breathing study PubMed 7741618 (carried); press-specific advice Not found

conditionCautions.change: Resistance training 2-3 non-consecutive days a week is recommended; usual glucose checks and fast carbohydrate on hand if on insulin or sulfonylureas; check feet and shoes; start light
conditionCautions.source: ADA position statement 2016, secondary summary (PMC5317029, carried; PMC2992214 snippet); press-specific advice Not found

conditionCautions.change: Only with clearance and a plan; very light loads, no breath-holding, stop with chest discomfort, dizziness or breathlessness
conditionCautions.source: ACE HIIT for clinical populations (carried, snippet); press-specific clearance Not found

conditionCautions.change: Fits regular exercise advice; start light and build up
conditionCautions.source: AHA recommendations (carried); press-specific advice Not found

conditionCautions.change: Floor press on a mat (check you can get down and up easily; a bench may be easier), light weight, 60-90 s rest; build gradually; combine with walking
conditionCautions.source: ACSM weight position stand (Donnelly 2009, carried); press-specific advice Not found

conditionCautions.change: Standard strength guidance applies; start with 2 sets and build
Train as usual if controlled; start light if fatigued; stop for palpitations or faintness
Warm up, reliever nearby; strength work is usually well tolerated; stop and use the reliever if wheeze or cough starts
conditionCautions.source: Asthma UK tips via Pharmacy Magazine CPD (carried); PubMed 21811185 (carried)

conditionCautions.change: The press puts little load on the knees; bent knees are fine on the floor, or keep the legs on a bench or use a chair if getting down is hard; stop with sharp or increasing pain
conditionCautions.source: Press-specific knee guidance Not found; Vanderbilt knee OA handout (carried)

conditionCautions.change: Floor press with knees bent, no arching, light weight; stop if pain increases or spreads down a leg; get advice if pain persists
conditionCautions.source: Coaching sources (aaptiv, boxrox, bodybuilding.com, snippets); clinical guidance specific to the press Not found

conditionCautions.change: Floor press for limited depth, elbows tucked, pain-free range, light weight; stop with pinching or pain and ask a physiotherapist; avoid if there is an acute injury
conditionCautions.source: Noteboom et al. 2024 PubMed 38974522 (snippet; model-based, healthy athletes); Myprotein and Fitbod floor press pages (coaching snippets); clinical guidance specific to the press Not found

conditionCautions.change: Loaded strength training is generally recommended for bone; keep the trunk still; with severe osteoporosis or a vertebral fracture get individual advice first
conditionCautions.source: PMC9304091 (carried, snippet); RACGP HANDI exercise for bone loss (carried, snippet); Brooke-Wavell et al. 2022 (carried)

conditionCautions.change: Ask your obstetrician or midwife; avoid long periods flat on the back later in pregnancy (use an incline or seated press); stop with dizziness, headache, pain, leaking or heaviness
conditionCautions.source: ACOG FAQ via secondary summary (snippet); PubMed 30337348 systematic review (snippet); Mayo Clinic pregnancy exercises (carried); ACOG's own wording Not found

conditionCautions.change: Ask a women's health physiotherapist; start with light weight and breathing; stop with leaking, heaviness or pain
conditionCautions.source: Goom, Donnelly and Brockwell 2019 (carried); NHS Lothian DRAMs (carried)

conditionCautions.change: Only with surgeon or physiotherapist approval, especially after shoulder, neck, chest, breast or abdominal surgery
